mainTopic: עירוב תחומין: the man and his son's directions, an עירוב just outside the city, and when a city counts as four אמות
overview: This amud finishes the משנה about עירוב תחומין and then explains it. First, the גמרא clarifies the case of a man who sends his son to place an עירוב 'to the east' or 'to the west.' If the directions are measured from his house, the house always sits between him and the עירוב, and one of the משנה's cases becomes impossible. רבי יצחק answers that the directions are measured from the son. רבא בר רב שילא answers instead that the house may stand on a diagonal. Next, the גמרא corrects the משנה's wording: an עירוב that works is one placed outside the city's outskirts (עיבור), not outside the תחום. A ברייתא says such a person can lose the whole city, not just what he gained. The גמרא resolves this by asking where his 2000 אמות run out, in the middle of the city or at its far end, and supports the answer with רבי יהושע בן לוי's rule. רבי אידי calls that rule 'words of prophecy.' רבא starts to show that a משנה teaches both cases, and his proof continues on the next amud.

steps.title: End of the משנה: what he gains on one side, he loses on the other
steps.stepSummary: The משנה closes its rule about an עירוב placed just outside the city: the distance gained on one side is lost on the opposite side.
steps.whatsHappening: These are the last words of the משנה. They describe someone whose עירוב sits just outside the city, beyond its outskirts (the עיבור). Steps 6–7 explain that this is the correct reading of the משנה's wording.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the עירוב is outside the city's area, his 2000 אמות are measured from the עירוב instead of from the city. He can walk farther in the direction of the עירוב. He loses the same distance in the opposite direction, because his 2000-אמה circle has shifted.

keyTerms.meaning: gains, profits
loses
food placed to set a new 'home base' for measuring the 2000 אמות one may walk on שבת

steps.whatToRemember: An עירוב does not add walking distance. It only moves the center of a person's 2000-אמה circle.

phrases.english: What he gains, he loses.
phrases.notes: He gains on the side where the עירוב is, but loses on the opposite side.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Conclusion of the משנה, which began on the previous amud
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An עירוב placed just outside the city (beyond its עיבור) shifts the person's 2000-אמה range, so whatever is gained on one side is lost on the other.

steps.title: The גמרא's first assumption: east and west of his house
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens with a working assumption: 'east' and 'west' in the משנה are measured from the man's house.
steps.simpleTranslation: The גמרא: You might think 'to the east' means east of his house, and 'to the west' means west of his house.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא states a first assumption about the משנה's words. This line sets up the question that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On this reading, the man stands on one side of his house and the עירוב is on the other side. That puts his house between him and his עירוב. The question in the next step depends on this picture.

keyTerms.meaning: it enters your mind / you might think (an initial assumption that will later be corrected)
to the east
to the west

steps.confusionAlert: קא סלקא דעתך is not the גמרא's final view. It is a temporary assumption that will soon be overturned.

phrases.english: GEMARA:
It might enter your mind:
'To the east' means east of his house.
'To the west' means west of his house.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the earlier case in the משנה, about the man and his son, to define its terms
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Initial assumption: the directions in the משנה are measured relative to the man's house, so his house lies between him and his עירוב.

steps.title: How can the עירוב be closer than his house?
steps.stepSummary: If the house is between the man and his עירוב, the משנה's second case is impossible. The עירוב cannot be within 2000 אמות while the house is farther away.
steps.simpleTranslation: The first case is understandable: his house is 2000 אמות from him and his עירוב is farther. You can find that, since he reaches his house but not his עירוב. But the second case says his עירוב is 2000 אמות from him and his house is farther. How can that happen?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the assumption from step 2. It shows that one of the משנה's two cases cannot happen under that picture.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the house is in the middle, the house is always closer to him than the עירוב. So 'house close, עירוב far' works fine. 'עירוב close, house far' cannot happen, yet the משנה gives a ruling for it.

keyTerms.meaning: granted / this part is fine (sets up 'but the other part is difficult')
you can find it (the case is possible)
how can you find it? (how is this case possible?)
2000 אמות, the walking limit (תחום) on שבת

phrases.english: Granted,
'from him to his house is two thousand cubits
and to his eiruv is more than this' —
you can find it,
since he reaches his house
and does not reach his eiruv.
But 'from him to his eiruv is two thousand cubits
and to his house is more than this' —
how can you find it?
phrases.notes: The puzzle is that his house sits between him and the עירוב, so the house should be closer.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the assumption made in step 2
steps.kashyaTarget: The assumption that 'east' and 'west' are measured from the man's house
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the house is always between him and the עירוב, the משנה's case of a close עירוב and a far house cannot happen.

steps.title: רבי יצחק: east and west of his son
steps.stepSummary: רבי יצחק rejects the assumption. The directions are measured from the son, who places the עירוב, not from the house.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יצחק said: Do you think 'to the east' means east of his house and 'to the west' means west of his house? No. 'To the east' means east of his son, and 'to the west' means west of his son.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יצחק answers the question by changing the reference point of 'east' and 'west' from the house to the son.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the directions are measured from the son, the house no longer has to sit between the man and his עירוב. Sometimes the עירוב will be closer to him and the house farther. That makes the משנה's second case possible.

keyTerms.meaning: do you think? (introduces a rejection of the questioner's assumption)
his son (who places the עירוב for him)

steps.whatToRemember: The question came from assuming the directions were measured from the house. Measuring from the son removes the problem, so both cases in the משנה are possible.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yitzchak said:
Do you think
'to the east' means east of his house,
'to the west' means west of his house?!
No, 'to the east' means east of his son,
'to the west' means west of his son.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 3 by rejecting the assumption of step 2
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefinition of the case: a new reference point for the directions
steps.terutzHavaAmina: East and west are measured from the man's house, so the house is always between him and the עירוב.
steps.terutzMaskana: East and west are measured from the son, so the עירוב can be closer than the house, and both cases in the משנה can happen.

steps.title: A second answer: the house stands on a diagonal
steps.stepSummary: רבא בר רב שילא keeps the original assumption that east and west are measured from the house. He answers the problem by picturing the house on a diagonal line.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא בר רב שילא said: You can even say that 'to the east' means east of his house and 'to the west' means west of his house. The case is where his house stands on a diagonal.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second answer to the problem from step 3. This answer does not reject the assumption that directions are measured from the house.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 3 assumed the house sits on the straight line between the man and his עירוב, so the man would have to be farther from the עירוב than from his house. רבא בר רב שילא says the house can sit off to the side, on a diagonal. Then the man is west of the house and the עירוב is east of it, but the man can still be closer to the עירוב than to the house.

keyTerms.meaning: A diagonal; a slanted line off to the side
East of his house
West of his house
For example; the case is where

steps.confusionAlert: Do not picture the man, the house, and the עירוב on one straight line. Picture a triangle: the house is up at the top, the man is down on the left, and the עירוב is down on the right. The man and the עירוב can be close to each other even though they are on opposite sides of the house.

phrases.english: Rava bar Rav Sheila said:
You can even say 'to the east' means east of his house,
and 'to the west' means west of his house,
for example, where his house stands on a diagonal.
phrases.notes: The house is off to the side, so the man and the עירוב can still be near each other.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different answer to the קשיא of step 3 than רבי יצחק gave in step 4
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the physical layout of the case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Measuring from the house makes the משנה's second case impossible
steps.terutzMaskana: Measuring from the house works if the house sits on a diagonal

steps.title: Can the משנה really mean 'outside the תחום'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה about placing an עירוב inside the city's outskirts. It asks how the משנה could speak of an עירוב placed outside the תחום.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'One who places his עירוב within the outskirts, etc.' Could you think it means outside the תחום?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה and challenges its wording. This sets up a correction in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An עירוב placed outside a person's 2000-אמה limit (תחום) is out of reach, so it cannot work at all. Yet the משנה treats an עירוב 'outside the תחום' as working. The wording therefore cannot be taken literally.

keyTerms.meaning: The city's outskirts: a strip of about 70 אמות around the city that counts as part of the city
Outside the 2000-אמה שבת limit
Could it enter your mind? (a challenge to an impossible reading)
Etc.; the quotation continues

phrases.english: 'One who places his eiruv within its outskirts, etc.'
Could you think it means outside the Shabbat limit?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves away from the east/west discussion to a new line of the משנה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: An עירוב beyond a person's תחום is unreachable, so it cannot work. The משנה cannot mean that literally.

steps.title: Corrected reading: 'outside the outskirts'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא corrects the wording to 'outside the עיבור'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its own challenge by correcting the משנה's wording.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה really means an עירוב placed just beyond the city's outskirts, still well within reach. An עירוב placed there works and moves the person's שבת base out of the city. An עירוב placed inside the outskirts does nothing, because that area counts as part of the city.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, say (introduces a corrected reading)
Outside the city's outskirts

phrases.english: Rather, say: outside its outskirts.

steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה speaks of an עירוב outside the תחום
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה speaks of an עירוב just outside the עיבור

steps.title: Does he lose only what he gains?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes 'what he gains he loses' and questions whether the loss is really that small.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'What he gains, he loses.' Only what he gains, and no more?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the משנה's rule and challenges it. This prepares for a ברייתא that says otherwise.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה suggests the loss on one side exactly equals the gain on the other side. The גמרא doubts that the loss is limited this way. It hints that the person may lose much more.

keyTerms.meaning: And no more? (questions whether something is really limited)

phrases.english: 'What he gains, he loses.'
Only what he gains, and no more?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns to the next phrase of the משנה
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's rule that the loss equals the gain
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The loss may be far larger than the gain, as the next step shows.

steps.title: A ברייתא: he can lose the whole city
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that an עירוב placed even one אמה outside the outskirts gains that אמה but loses the whole city, because the city now counts within his 2000 אמות.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught in a ברייתא: One who places his עירוב within the city's outskirts has done nothing. If he placed it outside the outskirts, even one אמה, he gains that אמה and loses the entire city, because the city's size is counted in his תחום.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא as the source for its challenge. The ברייתא describes a much bigger loss than the משנה does.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When his base is in the city, his 2000 אמות begin at the edge of the city, so the whole city is free. When his base moves outside the city, the 2000 אמות start from the עירוב, and walking across the city uses up those אמות. So he gains one אמה but may lose the entire city's length, which looks like it contradicts the משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: He did nothing at all
The size of the city
Is counted for him; is included

phrases.english: But it was taught:

phrases.aramaic: הַנּוֹתֵן אֶת עֵירוּבוֹ בְּתוֹךְ עִיבּוּרָהּ שֶׁל עִיר,
phrases.english: One who places his eiruv within the outskirts of the city,
has done nothing at all.
If he placed it outside the outskirts of the city,
even one cubit,
he gains that cubit
and loses the entire city,
because the measure of the city
is counted for him within the measure of the limit!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Provides the source behind the challenge in step 8
steps.raayaObject: The claim that the loss can be much greater than the gain
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא stating that he loses the entire city

steps.title: Different cases: where his 2000 אמות run out
steps.stepSummary: There is no contradiction. The ברייתא speaks of a case where his 2000 אמות end in the middle of the city. The משנה speaks of a case where they end at the far end of the city.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is not difficult. Here, his measure ended in the middle of the city. There, his measure ended at the end of the city.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא resolves the contradiction between the משנה and the ברייתא by assigning them to two different cases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the city is large and his 2000 אמות run out in the middle of it, he loses part of the city and everything past it, which is a big loss (the ברייתא). If his 2000 אמות stretch to the far end of the city, he only loses on that side about as much as he gained on the other (the משנה). Both sources are correct, each in its own case.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not difficult; there is no contradiction
Here... there (assigning each source to a different case)
His measure (of 2000 אמות) ran out

steps.whatToRemember: An עירוב placed just outside a city moves a person's שבת base, so the city itself now counts against his 2000 אמות. How much he loses depends on where those 2000 אמות run out: at the far end of the city he loses only about what he gained, but in the middle of the city he loses much more.

phrases.english: It is not difficult:
here, where his measure ended in the middle of the city,
there, where his measure ended at the end of the city.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in steps 8 and 9
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה and the ברייתא disagree about how much he loses
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא is where his measure ends mid-city, and the משנה is where it ends at the city's end

steps.title: Support from רבי יהושע בן לוי: middle of the city versus end of the city
steps.stepSummary: The answer in Step 10 matches רבי יהושע בן לוי's rule. If the measurement ends in the middle of the city, he gets only half the city. If it ends at the far edge, the whole city counts as four אמות and he gets the rest of his distance beyond it.
steps.simpleTranslation: And this follows רבי אידי, who said in the name of רבי יהושע בן לוי: if someone was measuring his 2000 אמות and the measurement ran out in the middle of the city, he has only half the city. If it ran out at the far end of the city, the whole city is treated as if it were four אמות, and he is given the rest of his distance beyond it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a teaching that supports its answer from Step 10. That answer said the result depends on where in the city his 2000 אמות end.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 10 said that the ברייתא is about 2000 אמות that end in the middle of the city, and the משנה is about 2000 אמות that end at the far edge. רבי יהושע בן לוי teaches exactly this split. If only part of the city falls inside his limit, he walks only as far as the measurement reaches. If the whole city falls inside it, the city shrinks to four אמות, and the distance he did not use continues on the far side.

keyTerms.meaning: Measuring along, counting out his 2000 אמות
His measurement ran out, meaning the 2000 אמות ended
The middle of the city
As if it were only four אמות, so the whole city counts as one small space
They give him the rest of his distance past the city

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the rule behind the whole סוגיא. A city counts as 'four אמות' only if all of it lies inside his limit.

phrases.english: And this is in line with Rabbi Idi,

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר רַבִּי אִידִי אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי:
phrases.english: for Rabbi Idi said that Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said:
If he was measuring along
phrases.notes: He is measuring his 2000 אמות from his שבת base outside the city.

phrases.english: and his measurement ran out in the middle of the city,
he has only half the city.
If his measurement ran out at the far end of the city,

phrases.aramaic: נַעֲשֵׂית לוֹ הָעִיר כּוּלָּהּ כְּאַרְבַּע אַמּוֹת,
phrases.english: the whole city becomes for him like four אמות,
and they give him the rest of his distance.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִדְרַבִּי אִידִי, דְּאָמַר רַבִּי אִידִי אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the answer in Step 10 by showing an אמורא who already made the same distinction.
steps.raayaObject: The answer that the ברייתא is about 2000 אמות ending in the middle of the city, and the משנה is about 2000 אמות ending at its far edge
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי יהושע בן לוי, as passed on by רבי אידי

steps.title: רבי אידי questions the logic of the distinction
steps.stepSummary: רבי אידי calls the rule 'words of prophecy,' meaning he cannot see the reasoning behind it. Why should it matter whether the measurement ends in the middle of the city or at its edge?
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אידי said: These are just words of prophecy. What difference does it make to me whether it ended in the middle of the city or at the far end of the city?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אידי challenges the very rule he just passed on. He cannot see why the two cases should be treated differently.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His question is basically this: in both cases the city stands inside his walking area. Why should the city shrink to four אמות only when the measurement happens to land exactly at its far edge? Calling the rule 'prophecy' means it looks like a rule with no logic behind it.

keyTerms.meaning: Words of prophecy, meaning a statement whose reasoning cannot be seen
What difference is it to me? A way of saying two cases should be the same

steps.confusionAlert: Do not get mixed up. The same רבי אידי who passed on רבי יהושע בן לוי's rule is the one now questioning it. He reported what he heard faithfully, but he did not understand the reasoning.

phrases.english: Rabbi Idi said:
These are nothing more than words of prophecy.
What difference is it to me if it ran out in the middle of the city,
or if it ran out at the far end of the city?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the reasoning of the source brought as support in Step 11.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יהושע בן לוי's distinction between a measurement ending in the middle of the city and one ending at its far edge
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The city is inside his walking area in both cases, so there seems to be no reason to treat them differently.

steps.title: רבא: a משנה already teaches both cases
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers that this is not a rule without reasoning, because a משנה teaches both cases. The first case is that people of a large city may walk through an entire small city.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: We learned both of them in a משנה: the people of a large city may walk through the entire small city.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא defends רבי יהושע בן לוי's rule by showing it is already written in a משנה. He begins quoting that משנה here, and the quote continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Picture a small city that lies completely inside the 2000 אמות of the people from the large city. Their measurement reaches the far end of the small city, so the whole small city counts as four אמות and they may walk all of it. That is the 'far end of the city' case. The 'middle of the city' case comes in the משנה's next line, on the next amud.

keyTerms.meaning: We learned both of them, meaning both cases are taught in a משנה
A large city
A small city
They may walk through

steps.whatToRemember: A city counts as four אמות only when all of it is inside a person's 2000 אמות. If the measurement ends partway through the city, he may walk only as far as the measurement reaches. רבא shows this comes from a משנה.

phrases.english: Rava said: We learned both of them in a mishna:
The people of a large city
may walk through the entire small city.
phrases.notes: The small city lies completely inside their limit, so it counts as four אמות.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי אידי's challenge from Step 12 by pointing to a משנה.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Pointing to a משנה that already contains the distinction
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי אידי thought the distinction had no source and no reasoning.
steps.terutzMaskana: A משנה teaches both cases. When a city lies completely inside one's limit, the whole city may be walked. The partial case comes in the משנה's next clause.
